review:
Battlefield 2042 changed my life.

The Battlefield franchise has been one of my top favourites for years, and I have loved every game they have put out, even BFV and Hardline. I was known among my friends as "the Battlefield guy". I honestly didn't think they could ever make a bad game, because they have the technology, resources, and experience that they've been building upon since 2002. In theory, they could just copy and paste a lot of the assets and systems they make and improve upon them with each new iteration.

With the announcement of BF 2042 I was extremely excited. Everything that was talked about up to the launch had me excited, and it was really looking like this was going to be the ultimate BF game. The atmosphere with the marketing and design was perfect, I fully expected it to be like BF1 but in a slightly futuristic setting. Boy was I wrong.

This game actually got me so depressed that it turned me off from gaming in general and made me take a good look at my life, it made me realize that if a game can make me this devastated then I need to make some changes. So I've been doing other things, such as going for walks and hikes regularly, working on personal projects, and improving my life in general. So thank you DICE, for making such as terrible game and destroying one of my favourite franchises of all time, it has really improved my life.

UPDATE:

My son actually enjoyed the game, so he played it a lot. I've completely changed my lifestyle. I bought a Tacoma and go offroading and camping regularly, I also work out regularily and am in the best shape of my life. I bought a house with 165 acres of land and started a side business while working my dream job full time. I still play games every once in a while, but it's no longer a focus. It's funny looking back at this review and the fact that it's because of this that my life has changed so drastically, I don't know if that's sad or profound, but I couldn't be happier with life than I am now.

It seems clear that there was a lack of focus from the top on figuring out what this game should be. Coming from someone who bought BF1942 when it was new, and has played every BF entry since then, I am disappointed. The amount of weapons and customization at launch shows an obvious path to some battlepass type mechanic in order to lock you into additional purchases and microtransactions.

The wide open maps are an absolute meat grinder for playing infantry. I don't know how many times I've chosen a spawn point and been immediately obliterated by vehicles. If you don't happen to get a vehicle when you first start a map, you need to hike for 300+ meters before getting to the first capture point on conquest.

There are no infantry focused maps at launch for the base game. Jumping into Portal allows certain options, but you can't progress unlocks or playercard options from this mode. If you hope to come across a chaotic boots on the ground "Metro" style map, you'll be disappointed.

The environments lack the subtle details from previous entries that allowed you to be immersed into the fight, and made you feel like you were actually in an intense battle. By contrast, the maps feel very flat to BFV or even BF1. Even the sound design doesn't have the same impact. You will frequently hear footsteps of another soldier that appear to be around the corner but are actually 50+ meters away.

You will be killed by SMG's at distance, even if you get the drop on someone with an AR or DMR (this is after the most recent patch). Essentially, if you don't use an SMG then prepare to lose most gunfights. 

In the Beta you were able to make wild moves with the helicopters to avoid incoming AA missiles, that when executed properly, made you feel like a veteran pilot. Now, if you're locked on and out of flares, God speed little buddy.

I'm not even going to list all of the mechanics that were a part of previous games that didn't make the cut, there are plenty of other gamers who have expressed this. All in all, I do have hope that the hard working developers can turn this around, but it could have easily had an additional year in development to get it right. I guess you have to build for shareholders somehow?

I'll continue to play since I have friends who want to jump into games here and there, but I will not enjoy it for the time being, and that makes me sad.

I'll put about as much effort into my review, as the devs put into this game.

The use of BitDefender and other third-party antivirus software suites, even reputable ones, will eventually run the risk of getting you Game Banned.

How, exactly? Well, if your antivirus software happens to have an active Online Threat Prevention mechanism—the kind that intervenes when a suspicious page or page element is connected to and loaded, to block it right then—it will cause EA Anticheat's Game Service process to repeatedly hang on launch, and intermittently drop and lose packets during a match and in general. All while you, the player, write it off as being the game's fault or your system hardware's fault, unknowingly having a ticking countdown timer of eventually being surprised by getting Game Banned for Cheating by specifically Using Software for Causing Service Disruption...Of yourself. And the connection you had to the game servers.

How is this problem dealt with, so that you never run into the issue I did? Well, one must specifically create an exception for the file path [b]C:/Program Files/EA/AC/EAAnticheat.GameService.exe[/b] within the antivirus software's Online Threat Prevention, or similarly named feature set list. If you created a generic exception for this program, you are still not safe. It must explicitly be toggled to be an exception targeting the Online Threat Prevention feature; not generic scanning of it.

If you did this process correctly, as an added bonus, you may find that the infinite startup movie launching bug happens far less often, or not at all. This might even be the true fix of it. No extra Windows Defender Firewall rules necessary beyond what was automatically prompted about. (Reset your Firewall rules to Defaults if you like, by the way. Just to be safe.)

Windows Security and Microsoft Defender are assumed to not require setting this given they are Microsoft products. Certainly not Windows Security given it is the bare essentials of antivirus protection in Windows.
—
Extra Update: Create General Scan Exceptions for the Documents/Battlefield 2042 folder path (This is where the game saves its user profile settings), and the C:/Program Files/EA/AC folder path (The EA Anticheat general Game Service location) to be extra sure that the game is not as likely to hang on launching.

It may still have a chance to hang even after all of this, but maybe a little less so.

So, this is yet another game and franchise that was ruined by corporate greed and ambition. It had a rough start, with numerous bugs, missing features, and overall poor design decisions. I missed much of the initial chaos and played mostly after the major fixes, so my perspective might be a bit biased. However, when I finally tried it, the game was already fun and improved significantly over the years. They fixed and redesigned many problematic aspects, added new content, and ironed out most of the bugs. I didn't encounter any noticeable issues during my ≈70 hours of gameplay. The gameplay is solid now, definitely capable of delivering those classic battlefield™ moments. It's just a shame that the destruction aspect was downgraded so much. Once a staple of the franchise, it's now taken a backseat. Environmental hazards like tornadoes are fun occasionally, but they should complement, not replace, the great destruction mechanics (and possibly Levolution also).

One aspect that is rarely mentioned is the potential of its theme and setting. Its uniqueness and potential were sadly overlooked, as it's essentially only represented by some text in the menus, overshadowed by cheesy, cringe-worthy character dialogues. Surprisingly, I found the music to be a highlight. It offers a unique and interesting take on Battlefield's iconic and beloved themes, composed by a really talented musician. Overall, it's a real shame. This game had potential, but it was undercooked and almost immediately disregarded. Support for Portal and BR modes was dropped almost from the start, and now the game itself is reaching its end. So, if you like Battlefield or multiplayer shooters in general, definitely give it a try while it's still possible, especially considering how cheap it can be now (or even free with an EA subscription).

It certainly has a lot of problems, from the awful launch, to the lack of initial direction, and the removal of legacy features that had to be added in post-launch, plus the rushed and last minute story that is somehow less interesting than 3 and 4's.
That being said, the core gameplay is as polished and as refined as Hardline and 5's, the simple changes to the formula with the new classes and abilities drastically change the regular play style, and the maps where 128 players can function properly are genuinely enjoyable. 
Given that this game is now in end-of-life, if you can pick this up for cheap, it is a blast to play with pals, and you can have genuine fun. Battlefield is a very difficult formula to screw up in one game.
That being said, if you want the best Modern Warfare experience, then stick with Battlefield 4

[h1] To summarize, 2042 is bad because the game is a terrible execution of a terrible vision. [/h1]

It's clear 2042 wanted to capitalize on the smash hit that was MW2019. Thematically, the hyper-modern tactical retention reloads and the contemporary-ish feel sold well. Financially, making nearly every soldier a named operator with unique dialogue and personality opened the door for massive amounts of monetization. Warzone, while being a separate beast, still lumbers on despite being plagued by hackers for nearly a year.

The janky weapon reloads in 2042 are a far-cry from the butter-smooth ones of 2019, and don't compare favorably to BF4 or BF1 in terms of consistency. It's as if the professionalism of the soldier reloading changes from weapon to weapon, and reeks of poor management of the animation team. The Portal reloads are especially inconsistent, and it was heartbreaking to see my BF3 M16A3 do an inane mag retention reload.

Their attempt to one-up the five-item weapon customization of MW2019 comes in the form of hot-swapping attachments. I don't think anyone asked for this feature, I don't think it adds anything to the game, and to be honest it feels like someone saw the difference between BF3 and BF4 and took away only that [b]The Players Like More Stuff. [/b] It also means that attachments can only come in one of four categories, and you can't start off rounds with your favorite attachments already applied. It conflicts with having swappable magnification sights too, so it's an inelegant and limiting design choice made just for the trailer.

The operators and class system are perhaps a more egregious error. Gone are the classes and class-specific gadgets of the older titles - now you can choose an operator that heals in conjunction with the kit that gives you ammo, or the grapple hook and a launcher, etc. Class distinction is muddied and you can't tell who has what ability based on just looking at them. It's also a visual train wreck. At least 5 had the enemy as a readily identifiable opposite faction. In 2042 the only distinction between your team and the enemy is that the enemy speaks the other language (Russian or English) and don't have a blue icon over their head.

The character of the operators themselves might be acceptable. They're inoffensive at least, and the cosmetics are about as outlandish as MW2019 got, just that they have weird things on release. Separating head and body cosmetics is neat, but the UI looks like a free to play mobile game with how they point to your blue-tier cosmetics being way inferior to the super rare pink ones. Also it exists to bleed you of money, so there's that.

I thought it was interesting and potentially cool that they tied specific knives to specific execution animations, but the executions are in third person which for personal aesthetic reasons is bad. I get that it's to show off the fancy animations and your stupid season 4 bunny outfit, but it sucks.

The shooting feels like BF4, so no real step forward since 8 years ago. Combined with the worse maps and the worse class situation, it's an overall inferior experience to an 8 year old game. Some people say the bloom is worse, which it might be.

I can't comment on the call-ins of tanks and vehicles other than to say that it seemed like a stupid gimmick and the maps made roaming in the deadzones between objectives seem like an easy way to farm kills.

The conquest maps are mostly empty fields with small pockets of limited cover around the objectives. You're going to end up fighting over those anyway so the large maps mean the places you fight over are more boring than BF4 and now there's a half-minute second run through empty space between the current skirmish and the next. Why make a map larger if you're going to end up putting less stuff in it anyways?

[b] Hint: [/b] [spoiler] They're adding a battle royale mode and that's going to be their main selling point going forward. They don't actually care about the multiplayer and that's why they invested so much in the Portal minigames at the expense of the main game. [/spoiler]

As a hardcore Battlefield fan with thousands of hours spent on all previous Battlefield titles I can confidently say that this the current bottom of the decline in the franchise which started after BF4. This is NOT a Battlefield game, this is an EA watered down shit-show imitation.

That said, here is precisely why I do NOT recommend this game:

- There are very few weapons in the game and only a few of them work as they should. The automatic weapons have horrible RNG shooting mechanics where the bullets spread everywhere regardless of recoil, ARs are completely useless, SMGs are laser beams even in long range. Everyone is playing with PP as it beats every gun at almost all ranges.

- Weapon progression is non-existent. It is full of duplicate parts that you unlock which do the same thing with exact same stats like 4 silencers that have the exact same effect or 3 grips that have the same stats and effects.

- Customization UI/UX is horrible and takes away from the amazing feature that is in-match customization. There is no notification on the UI anywhere after you unlock parts, you have to search for them weapon by weapon. This entire feature also doesn't work in Portal modes where you need to setup each weapon 1 by 1 through the most incredibly unintuitive UI User Exeperiences I have ever had.

- Operators are OK in concept but the way they are portrayed is horrible, cringy, childish and does not fit this franchise at all. I hate every second I see them on the screen in 'character'.

- Score has been replaced by XP Gain and it doesn't reward you properly for the things that you do in the game to win the match. All the cool bonus points you used to get for stuff like Snipe Distance bonus have been removed. You can't tell how much damage you did to vehicles or what you have disabled. ALl you actions have been devolved into 5 ribbons which you somehow get anyway diminishing the achievements you did during the match.

- Squad Gameplay is nonexistent. Achievements that you made with your squad used give extra score, since that has been removed there is no incentive to play with your squad. Also squads can take only 4 people, can not be locked and can not be changed as willed. So you are either stuck with randoms or can jump to a random squad. 

- Spotting, squad ordering and all that stuff you used to do with Q do not work. You can't give or follow an order to get more points. This again destroys squad and any organized play.

- Vehicle physics are horrible. Especially Helicopters have been ruined. Helicopter controls have been watered down so much it feels like some stupid arcade game for 6 year olds. You can pitch or yaw an helicopter 45 degrees and it will stay at its position for so long before starting to drift.

- Vehicle balance is broken beyond comprehension. The 'basic' vehicles, jeep and hovercraft are INSANELY tanky and have crazy weapons AND can be called almost anytime. They literally take 4-5 rockets to kill and they can just drive away to AUTOREPAIR. They have the Attack Helicopter cannon on top, ALSO they can not damage eachother with their weapons SO they basically destroy infantry while infantry has no chance against them. This is amplified by the fact that maps are horrible.

- ALL MAPS are completely flat open spaces where there is nothing around to play with. As infantry you are just standing out in the open 90% of the time just to get farmed by invincible hovercrafts that have Apache Cannons on them. Whoever 'DESIGNED' those maps should quit their job if their title is anywhere close to level designer.

- Talking of quitting, that reminds me, EVER SINGLE PERSON THAT WORKED ON THE UI/UX OF THIS GAME SHOULD BE IMMEDIATELY FIRED ALONG WITH EVERYONE THAT TOOK A GOOD LOOK AND SAID 'OK EVERYTHING LOOKS GREAT LETS GO WITH THIS UI DESIGN'. There is so many icons in the game you can't see where you are aiming. I don't care about my teammates 400m away or that point 700m away that is being capped. When you open the Map, you literally can not find yourself because you are just the same triangle overlapped with the other 63 people with 2 additional pixels to distinguish yourself from. The customization UIs are horrible, with the part type on the left you can click but also displayed on the right with the + sign to add an attachment where you can NOT click, then you need to right click and hover over another attachment to swap etc. etc. It is SO bad it must have been a 'designed' by an intern. How this goes live is unbelievable.

- There is no squad play, no team play, there is nothing to incentivize players to play together. This is amplified by the fact that there are no classes and everyone can be self sufficient. No one wants to take to chance to rely on another player since they can already cover everything with their own build. The game feels empty and soulless where you spawn and try to go after your own agenda. 

- For Conquest horrible map design makes this worse as well since the maps are mostly EMPTY AND FLAT, the game devolves into teams splitting into two to fight over two objectives around the one or two points of interest on the map. There is no strategy, no holding a front, no team play. 

- At the end of the match you can not see what you have achieved. Everything is watered down to 5 ribbons which doesn't mean anything. All you get left with is the horribly cringy tik tok video of the operator you chose. 

This game CAN recover but I am not very optimistic because they need to improve:

[h1]FANS DESERVED BETTER THAN THIS[/h1]

Battlefield 2042 is the latest installment in the long-running Battlefield franchise, developed by DICE and published by Electronic Arts. Set in a near-future world on the brink of collapse, it aims to deliver a high-stakes, large-scale first-person shooter experience. Marketed as a return to form after the disappointment of Battlefield V, it instead fell short of expectations - arguably becoming an even bigger misstep for the series.
[b]As much as I’ve enjoyed the game since Season 5, I still can’t recommend it.[/b] Sure, the updates have been solid - DICE fixed, reworked, and added a lot of content - but it shouldn’t have taken so many months to get here. 
The game launched in a terrible state, comparable to the rocky premieres of Cyberpunk 2077 and Fallout 76. And even now, it still falls short in many areas when stacked against previous Battlefield titles. I do appreciate DICE’s commitment to improving the game - especially when you consider how quickly Battlefield V was abandoned - but it’s simply not enough. [b]DICE and EA: if you want players to leave positive reviews, try launching a GOOD and FINISHED product next time.[/b]

[b]Story[/b]
Disappointingly, there's no campaign mode at all.

[b]Game Modes[/b]
Conquest (64 and 128), Close Quarter Conquest (64), and Breakthrough (64) are really the only default game modes that matter. I personally play almost exclusively in CQC - it’s intense and fast-paced - but unfortunately, the map pool is limited to just three. If you're looking for more variety, larger maps, or vehicle gameplay, Conquest and Breakthrough still hold up well. No complaints from me on that front.
Occasionally, the game introduces special events with unique modes and rewards. While they can be hit or miss, they offer players a welcome change of pace and something fresh to experience.

[b]Portal[/b]
Battlefield Portal is an incredible concept that ultimately suffered from a lack of new content. It lets players create custom matches with a wide range of gameplay options and share them with the community. Overall, it's a fantastic feature that deserves to be a staple in future Battlefield games.

[b]Hazard Zone[/b]
Hazard Zone is essentially an extraction shooter, aiming to be a Tarkov-lite set in the Battlefield universe. Unfortunately, it failed to capture interest, and as a result, it faded away quickly.

[b]Specialists[/b]
I’m one of those players who couldn’t care less about the specialists. Do I think it was a bad idea that doesn’t fit the Battlefield formula? Absolutely. Does it make the game unplayable or even significantly less enjoyable? Not really.
On one hand, I like the idea of gadgets and unique traits for each operator, but on the other hand, it's a bit odd to see 20 Sundances in a single match. With a few adjustments, it could be a fun gimmick in future Battlefield games - just don't make it the core focus.

[b]Gunplay[/b]
Gunplay is always subjective, so I won’t spend too much time on it. Personally, I enjoyed it. It’s casual and doesn’t demand much mental effort - perfect for players who don’t have the time to master every nuance of the game. Most of the weapons are easy to handle, meaning even with average aim, you can still find yourself topping the leaderboards.
The TTK (time to kill) feels solid overall - fast enough to be satisfying, with the exception of three or four guns. As a result, enemies rarely feel like bullet sponges. That said, there are still issues with hit registration, lag spikes, and occasional desyncs. These problems can make the TTD (time to death) feel frustrating at times, as you can be one-shotted without any chance to fight back. While these issues aren’t as prevalent on smaller maps, they become much more noticeable in matches with 128 players.

[b]Vehicles[/b]
I don’t have much to say about the vehicles in BF2042, since I rarely use them. The controls feel clunky, the vehicles move awkwardly, and flying helicopters and jets isn’t all that satisfying.

[b]Server Browser[/b]
There’s no server browser, and it’s hard to understand why DICE was so determined not to include it. It remains one of the dumbest decisions they made.

[b]Destruction[/b]
Compared to older Battlefield games, this one feels like a step backward. Rather than enhancing the existing systems to allow for more impactful destruction, they scaled it back. Even visually, the explosions and building demolitions lack the satisfying impact we’ve come to expect.

[b]Maps[/b]
The maps in Battlefield 2042 are a real mixed bag - some, like Spearhead, are solid, while others, like Kaleidoscope, miss the mark. The release maps were especially bad before their reworks. They were too large, too open, with vast flat terrains and hardly any cover. Thankfully, most of them are now at least playable.
It might be controversial (or maybe not?), but I genuinely think the later maps from the new seasons are fantastic. Redacted especially stands out - it's easily one of my all-time favorites in the Battlefield franchise.

[b]HUD & UI[/b]
I like the overall design of the HUD. It’s modern, minimalist, and provides all the essential information without cluttering the screen (for the most part). Unfortunately, the customization options are limited, so if you’re not a fan of the default HUD, you're pretty much stuck with it.
After several patches, the UI has become much more solid. The menus have been streamlined, and even something as simple as changing attachments is no longer a hassle.

[b]Visuals[/b]
In my opinion, the game looks (mostly) good. While the older maps could use some improvement - often feeling too clean and lacking in detail - the newer ones are visually stunning. Redacted is packed with incredible detail, while Exposure impresses with its breathtaking environmental design.
The dynamic weather is an impressive concept, but in the long run, it doesn’t quite deliver. While random tornadoes or sandstorms can add unpredictability to fights, they often don’t feel impactful enough. It would be better if these events were rarer but capable of causing real havoc on the battlefield.

[b]Audio[/b]
Technically, the soundtrack isn't bad. It's solid electronic music with a subtle noise element. The problem, however, is that it doesn't suit the game. While it fits the theme, it doesn’t match the gameplay. What we need is something that hypes us up, something to pump adrenaline into our veins! This is an FPS, not a horror or sci-fi game.
The rest of the audio is decent. Nothing groundbreaking, but at least everything sounds as it should.

[b]Technicalities[/b]
Performance heavily depends on the map and game mode you're playing. From my experience, fewer players usually means better FPS and less desync. That’s why I’ve always avoided the 128-player mode - it’s essentially a technical nightmare. Interestingly, newer maps seem to be better optimized compared to the older or reworked ones. You'd expect better quality from maps that have so much extra work put into them...
There are still a fair number of bugs and glitches. Aside from major issues like wonky hit registration and lag spikes, there are also smaller problems - like falling under the map or encountering flying vehicles.
The game supports crossplay with consoles, but if you're not a fan, there's an option to disable it.
